deck.name: Mastering /design in Claude Code — video brief

claims.text: The previous path required sharing the design, pushing it into a Claude project, then copying the prompt and generated files into Claude Code by hand.
/design opens a multi-artboard canvas from one command typed in the project folder.
The skill designs only; it does not write the application code.
One prompt returned five design variations laid out on a single canvas.
Iterating on one direction means naming its artboard number, which leaves the other directions intact for comparison.
Elements are edited directly: hover to highlight, a properties panel, a live colour picker, text, and corner radius.
Hand-editing a colour is faster than prompting for it, because a prompt costs a full model turn.
The locally hosted site rendered without the two colour changes made on the canvas.
The cause was an un-pressed Save button in the top right of the canvas.
Canvas edits stay local until Save republishes the page, which is when the agent can read them.
The canvas is a published artifact page carrying both the editor and the artboards, not a panel embedded in Claude Code.
It is an early preview; the editor baked into a canvas does not update after publish.
Adopt one habit: prompt for structure, click for style, and Save before telling the agent anything changed.

slides.action_title: The canvas is native now. Your edits still aren't.
slides.audience_job: Understand in one line what changed and what still bites

speaker_notes.narrative: Source: Brendan Jowett, 'Master NEW /design Claude Skill In 10 Minutes!' (12:26).

slides.action_title: Prompt for structure, click for style, Save before you speak
